x: John Martin, 12 years, is quite a performer in his age group and a tower of strength for his school, virtually winning the points cup on his own. Colin Clair, 13½, the winner of the boys' competition, a lad of forward development for his age, may well prove to be a good all rounder.

The next event, the Shot Put, was held on 16th May and in spite of incessant pouring rain, six boys turned out and those who had competed last year, showed considerable improvment. Colin Clair, second last year, improved 8' 8" to take first place with a put of 26' 10".

Firstly we apologise to Colin Clair, the winner of the Boys' Shot put, for an incorrect result in the last issue, the distance should have been 35 ft. 6ins. and not 26 ft. 10ins. which was his figure for last year.

We also have a number of promising Juniors including Reg Chamberlain who got 2nd place in the Surrey Long Jump last year and we hope to see more Youths competing along with Colin Clair and Malcom Draper.
5 · C.E. Clair · (Bel.) · 17'6"

Colin Clair is with us once more and in addition to several good all round performances has thrown the javelin 190'11". Kenneth Silvester won the Pole Vault at our own Field Events Meeting at his first appearance in our colours.
Mel Batty won in 48:13.4 which was 3rd fastest time ever, behind Heatley and Zatopek. It's good to see Colin Clair back in the Belgrave fold again.
Derek Wade and Colin Clair had a real day out in the field events, taking three titles each. Derek took all three jumps and Colin the weight, Discus and javelin.
Generally, we had the edge on the track, whilst the Germans swept the field events - except for the senior javelin where Colin Clair's 186'4" was a worthy win.

Derek Wade had a great long jump of 22'-3½", which placed him second; he is surely destined to break the 23'-0" barrier shortly; and Colin Clair was also 2nd in the javelin with a good early-season throw of 176'-0".

…Gibson of Surrey A.C. - and Geoff North (14:44.4) and Bill Kerr (14:48.8) chasing Alan Perkins home in the 5000 metres. Colin Clair was our best placed field events man (4th), throwing the javelin 175'.2".…
Javelin · 1. · C. Clair · 178'0½"
Once again Colin Clair was our leading field events man, retaining his Discus and Javelin Titles, winning the high jump and finishing second in the weight.
From a run-up of a few yards he threw 207'7¾" - almost 20 feet further than Colin Clair's 1963 record. He also won the Shot and Discus with more modest marks.

In the Javelin, Brian King threw over 9'0" further than before to beat Colin Clair by only 1" with Barry Townsend 3rd. Brian's magnificent effort just halted Colin's bid for a treble as he took the discus and shot, both with best distances by Belgravians so far this year.

In this match we beat LAC by 15 points with the Irish Guards a further 16 points behind. Colin Clair put the shot 38'6" for 2nd place behind Gerry Davies(LAC) and John Martin was close to his best again with 36'10¼".

Good marks in the sprints and field events resulted in a pleasing win against these two strong clubs. Colin Clair and John Mitchell scored a one,two in the Shot with the former going on to grab 2nd place in the Javelin from Brian King, 3rd.
Javelin · 1. · C.Clair · 177'2"

Prior to the Javelin competition Colin Clair had joked about the possibility of his gaining a AAA Grade I Standard. No one was more suprised than he when on his 5th effort the spear reached well over the 200' line and was later measured at 210'2" - a standard and Club Honours Badge by 2" .
After the number of club trustees had been promptly reduced from five to four, honours badges were presented to: Seniors - C.Martin, C.Clair and J.Bicourt
Discus (108'3½") · 124'0" · C.Clair
Senior Club Records were set by John Thresher (2m), Barry Townsend (Decathlon) Malcolm Robinson (3m), Geoff North (3m), John Bicourt (3000mSC) and equalled by Colin Clair (Jav).
Alan Mead took second place with an inspired performance and his very best ever, closely followed by Tony Brooks. The furthest putt was by Colin Clair with 35'2½".
